extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, copyholders, compositors, and typesetters working on manuscripts and book/journal production
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for punctuation, hyphenation, word divisions, footnotes, indexing, tables, spacing, indentation, proofs, and production workflows for preparing manuscripts for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: General hyphen use
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyphen connects elements within words but 'must not look outside of manuscript tradition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some writers object to certain hyphen usages as foreign ('Teutonism'). Use hyphens according to the style conventions given in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphen to indicate prefixes or suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a hyphen to indicate a prefix or a suffix as a particle or syllable not complete in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The prefix a-'; 'The German diminutive suffixes -chert and -/e»n.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphen to indicate syllables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a hyphen to indicate the syllables of a word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: di-a-gram, pho-tog-ra-phy.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of common hyphenated words
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain everyday compound words should be hyphenated and do not fall under other classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: after-years, cross-section, page-proof, man-of-war, bas-relief, death-rate, pay-roll, object-lesson, birth-rate, feast-day, post-office, title-page, blood-relations, sea-level, wave-length, common-sense, fountain-head, sense-perception, well-being, cross-examine, guinea-pig, son-in-law, cross-reference, horse-power, subject-matter, will-power, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary divisions (word breaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid dividing words across lines unless necessary; carry the whole word into the next line wherever consistent with good spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer whole words when spacing allows; unnecessary hyphenation and divisions reduce readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dividing on two-letter syllables in wide measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In wide measures (20 ems or more), avoid dividing on a syllable of two letters if possible; good spacing is paramount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words of four letters (e.g., on-ly) should never be divided; five- or six-letter words rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit consecutive hyphenated line endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Never let more than two consecutive lines terminate in a hyphen, if at all avoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ending the next-to-last line of a paragraph with a divided word; the last line in measures of 15 ems and up should contain at least four letters. Try to avoid a broken word at the bottom of a recto (right-hand) page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not divide proper nouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not divide proper nouns, especially names of persons, unless absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep names intact across lines whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not separate initials or abbreviations across lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not separate the initials of a name, or combinations like a.d., P.M., etc., by putting parts on different lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep letter combinations and initials on the same line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep divisional marks with the section they precede
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid separating a divisional mark (e.g., (a) or (i)) in the middle of a sentence from the section it precedes; carry the mark over with its matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow such marks to fall at the end of a line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide according to pronunciation (American system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide words according to pronunciation, not derivation (American system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: democ-racy, not demo-cracy; kfwwl-edge (knowledge OCR oddity), not know-ledge; aurif-erous, not auri-ferous; antip-odes (better: antipodes), not anti-podes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide on etymological/derivational lines when compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: When compatible with pronunciation and good spacing, divide on etymological lines or according to derivation and meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: dis-pleasure is better than displeas-ure; school-master better than schoolmas-ter. Avoid forms like Passo-ver, diso-bedience, une-ven, disa-bled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid terminating a line in certain consonant sounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not terminate a line in a soft c or g, or in a ; (OCR artifact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unavoidable, divide so as to preserve readability: pro-cess, not proc-ess; ne-cessary, not nec-essary; spa-cing, not spacing (rule: present participles should carry -ing over); pro-geny not prog-eny; pre-judice not prej-udice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide on a vowel where practicable; exceptions for -able/-ible
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever practicable, divide on a vowel; if a vowel alone forms a syllable in the middle of a word, set it into the first line. Exceptions: words in -able and -ible should carry the vowel over into the next line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sepa-rate, not sep-arcUe; particu-lar, not partic-idar; read-able, not reada-ble; convertible, not converii-ble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid additional hyphens in already hyphenated words
rubrics_metrics.description: In hyphenated nouns and adjectives avoid adding further hyphens when dividing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: object-lesson, not object-lesson (i.e., avoid inserting a second hyphen split); fellow-being, not fel-low-being; poverty-stricken, not pov-erty-stricken or pov-erty-stricken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat diphthongs as one letter when dividing
rubrics_metrics.description: A coalition of two vowel sounds (a diphthong) should be treated as one letter; avoid dividing if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: peo-ple (either syllable makes bad division), Cae-sar, ailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of derivatives depends on accent shift
rubrics_metrics.description: In derivatives from words ending in -ct (OCR shows '/'), the 't' in divisions should be carried into the next line with the suffix if the accent has been shifted; if the derivative retains the parent-word accent, the 't' stays in the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: objee-tive (from ob'ject); defective (from defect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural -s does not justify new divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a plural s (creating a new syllable) does not justify dividing the original stem differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'horses' and 'circumstan-ces' are impossible divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide adjectives in -ical on the 'i'
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjectives ending in -ical should be divided on the 'i'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: physi-cal, not phys-ical or physic-al.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not divide the word 'nothing' (literal rule as stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not divide nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As given: 'Do not divide nothing.' (Keep 'nothing' intact.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use superior figures for reference indices (footnotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reference indices, as a rule use superior figures rather than asterisks, daggers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index figures in the text should be placed after punctuation marks; example illustrated. When figures are not used, the sequence of indices should be: * (asterisk), † (dagger), ‡ (double dagger), § (section mark), || (parallels), ¶ (paragraph mark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'ibid.' for closely following repeated references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where references to the same work follow each other closely and uninterruptedly, use 'ibid.' instead of repeating the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Ibid.' takes the place of as much of the previous reference as is repeated. Avoid using 'ibid.' as the first footnote on a verso page; prefer to repeat the title if short, or use 'loc. cit.' or 'op. cit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes to tables: placement and type size
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes to tables (ruled or open) should be in 6-pt and placed at the foot of the table, not the foot of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reference indices in tables use asterisks, daggers, etc., not superior figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not repeat author's name in footnote if given in text
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author's name is given in the text in connection with a reference or quotation, it should not be repeated in the footnote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'This theory is questioned by Herbert, as follows: "I cannot admit ..."¹' then footnote: 'Laws of the Ancients, I, 153.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Place index figure after quotation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is better to place the index figure (footnote marker) in the text after the quotation than before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use punctuation placement demonstrated in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit 'Vol.', 'chap.', 'p.' ordinarily in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily omit the abbreviations 'Vol.,' 'chap.,' and 'p.' in references to particular passages; use Roman numerals for Volume/Book/Part/Division (capitals), except classical works where lower-case roman is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Arabic numerals for numbers (Heft) and text pages. Use 'Vol.', 'p.' only when confusion likely. In classical references use periods instead of commas to separate divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of periodical follows volume number in parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: In a reference to a periodical, the date of publication should immediately follow the volume number and be put in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See illustrated examples in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote numbering for linotype-set matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In matter set on the linotype machine, footnotes should be numbered consecutively through an article (or chapter in a book) to save resetting in case of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: numbering per page causes resetting if sequence changes. Exceptions noted for specific journals which number per page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: treatment of particles (French/Spanish 'le, la, el', 'de', etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: French, Belgian, or Spanish names preceded by 'le,' 'la,' 'l',' du,' or 'des' should be listed under the letters of the prefix in advance of ordinary 'L' or 'D' list; if preceded by 'de' or 'd'' list under the first letter of the word following the prefix, placing the particle after initials or Christian name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Le Conte, John; La Noue, Francois de; L'Estrange, Sir Roger; Du Maurier, George; Des Essarts, Jean; Estrées Gabrielle d'; Rambeau, Emile de; La Mancha, Don Quixote de. Note: if particle is actually part of the surname, index according to particle: De Bey, Robert; De Quincey, Thomas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: German 'von' and similar particles
rubrics_metrics.description: German names preceded by 'von' should be indexed according to the initials of the name following the prefix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Stemthal, Max von; Goethe, J. W. von.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: treatment of M', Mac, Mc names
rubrics_metrics.description: Names beginning with 'M',' Mac,' or 'Mc' with the following letter capitalized should be indexed in advance of the ordinary 'M' list (section arranged alphabetically by letters following the 'M',' 'Mac',' or 'Mc'); names beginning with 'Mac' without the following letter capitalized should take their natural places in the 'Mac' list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow capitalization-sensitive ordering conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: treatment of O', St., Van with capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Names preceded by 'O',' 'St.,' or 'Van,' with the following letter capitalized, should be placed in advance of the 'O,' 'S' or 'V' lists and arranged alphabetically according to the letter following the particle; names beginning with 'Van' without following letter capitalized should take their ordinary places in 'V' list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example distinctions provided in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: names with connectives (and, &, y, et)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names having two parts or firm-names connected by 'and', '&', 'y' (Spanish), or 'et' (French) should be listed according to the first letter of the name preceding the connective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Smith and Evans (under 'S'); Gomez y Pineda, Liberie (under 'G'); Loubet et Meimier (under 'L').

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: hyphenated names English vs French
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenated names should be listed according to the name following the hyphen if English; according to the name preceding the hyphen if French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Taylor, Henry Chandler- (for Henry Chandler-Taylor); Saint-Saens, Charles Camille (for Charles Camille Saint-Saëns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table typography: point sizes for tables by body type size
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for type sizes in open and ruled tables depending on the surrounding matter (11-pt, 10-pt, 9-pt, 8-pt, 6-pt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In 11-pt and 10-pt matter open tables ordinarily set in 9-pt leaded; ruled in 8-pt solid. In 9-pt matter both open and ruled set in 8-pt solid. In 8-pt matter open tables set in 6-pt leaded; ruled in 6-pt solid. In 6-pt matter both open and ruled in 6-pt solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table captions and box-heads type size and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions for columns of open tables and box-heads for ruled tables should ordinarily be set in 6-pt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ruled tables with multi-story box-heads, primary heads set in caps and small caps; secondary heads in caps and lower-case. Wherever small caps used in box-heads, the stub (first column) head should be in caps and small caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table rule spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: In ruled tables there should be at least two leads (points) space between horizontal rules and the matter inclosed, and if practicable at least an en-quad between perpendicular rules and matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent breathing room between rules and table contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders and column separation in tables
rubrics_metrics.description: In open tables set by hand, use periods (one em apart and aligned) between the columns; when set on the linotype machine, use regular leaders. In ruled tables, use leaders in the stub if room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leader = piece of type with dots (period leader) or short lines (hyphen leader) used to guide the eye across spaces to the correct word or number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures alignment and leaders width
rubrics_metrics.description: In columns of figures, for blanks use leaders the width of the largest number in the column (e.g., for four digits use a 2-em leader); center the figures in the column; if unequal number of digits leave more space on left than right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure visual alignment and consistent leader widths appropriate to the largest group of digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-matter in table columns
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is reading-matter in columns of a ruled table, center it if possible; if any line runs over, use hanging indention and align all on the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hanging indent for multi-line cells and align consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set tables to even picas when practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables and individual columns should be set to even picas (or nonpareils) if practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes layout regular and easier to align across pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use double rules at the top of all tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Double rules should be used at the top of all tables; vertical rules used usually only when a table is doubled up on itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rule style conventions for table headers and overall table framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open vs ruled tables by column count
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables of two columns only should be set as open; three or more columns as ruled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler two-column tables avoid heavy ruling; multi-column data benefits from ruled structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Table I', etc., in headlines should ordinarily be set in caps of the same type as the body of the table; the descriptive line (if any) in caps and small caps of the same type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single descriptive headline without number should be set in caps of the body type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of typographic units (point system, ems, en)
rubrics_metrics.description: The point is the underlying unit of typographical measures; a pica = 12 points (one-sixth of an inch). Definitions of em-quad, en-quad, 3-em space, 4-em, 5-em, hair-space, em-dash, en-dash, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show common type sizes (12-pt pica, 11-pt small pica, 10-pt long primer, down to 5-pt pearl) and naming conventions. Use these units to set spacing and measures consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style names: roman, italic, bold-face and font composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary type is roman; sloping face is italic; heavy black face is bold-face. A font includes caps, small caps, and lower-case letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript indications: underline for italic, wavy-line for bold. Indicators for caps and small caps shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space evenly: standard interword and punctuation spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard line should have a 3-em space between words not separated by punctuation other than commas, and after commas; an en-quad after semicolons and colons followed by a lower-case letter; two 3-em spaces after colons followed by a capital; an em-quad after periods, exclamation, and question points concluding a sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reducing spacing, begin with commas and slanted-shoulder letters; if increasing, begin with overlapping-kern letters and straight-up letters; in a well-spaced line, most words should have 3-em space and the rest no more than an en-quad. Avoid alternating very thin and very wide spaced lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hair-spacing or em-quading to avoid runs
rubrics_metrics.description: Never hair-space, or em-quad, a line to avoid a run-over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use extreme micro-adjustments to force layout at the expense of even spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not space out last line of paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not space out the last line of a paragraph allowing an indention of an em or more at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unjustified raggedness produced by over-spacing last lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short words spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short words, like 'a', 'an', etc., should have the same space on each side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent optical spacing for short words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thin space uses and money formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a thin space after §, ff., and similar signs; before 'ff.' and metric symbols. In American and English money, no space is used between symbols ($, £) and numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '§14. Be it further ordained ...'; 'pp. 10 ff.'; '$2.75'; '£10 ss. 2d.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing after numerals for subsection heads and scripture refs
rubrics_metrics.description: After Arabic numerals at beginning of lines (subsections) use an en-quad; after Roman numerals, an em-quad. Scripture references spaced: II Cor. 1 : 16-20; 2 : 5 — 3 : 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow spacing rules for different numeral systems and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No space between letters in products and before super/subscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Between letters forming products, and before superior figures or letters indicating powers, and inferior figures or letters, ordinarily no space should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formulae shown; keep mathematical/chemical notations compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation measurements by measure width and point size
rubrics_metrics.description: Indentation amounts vary by measure width and type size: in measures <10 picas indent 1 em for all sizes; in measures 10–20 picas use specified em values per point size; in 20–30 picas use larger indent values. Separate rules for hanging indentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact table of indents given for 11-pt, 10-pt, 9-pt, 8-pt, 6-pt matter for plain and hanging paragraphs; apply the listed em values per the measure width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry indentation and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: For poetry center the longest line and govern indentation by that (or average of long lines if one is disproportionate). Indent according to rhyme and line length; align blank verse; align consecutive rhyming lines; indent alternately rhyming lines similarly; indent disproportionately short lines more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple quotations from different poems vary slightly in line length, indent all alike. Examples and a sample stanza illustrate recommended alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph kinds: prefer plain paragraphs for reading-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish plain (first line indented; others flush) and hanging paragraphs (first line flush; others indented). Plain paragraphs are preferable for ordinary reading-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hanging indention to emphasize opening words, numbers, or when center-heads span more than three lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of proof types (galley, page, plate, foul, revise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Galley-proof: impression of type in galley; page-proof: impression made up into page form; plate-proof: proof taken of type-page before electrotype cast; foul proof: galley-proof containing author's corrections; revise: new proof corrected from a marked proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand differences because handling, correction stage, and costs differ across proof types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up and folio conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make-up = arranging type-lines into page-form. A folio is a page-number: even numbers on verso, odd on recto. A drop-folio is a page-number at the bottom of a page. Half-title or bastard title = abbreviated title on a separate page preceding full title-page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow folio placement conventions consistently across the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linotype and monotype machine descriptions (production constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linotype and monotype composing machines operate differently with implications for corrections and resetting: linotype produces slugs (lines) and requires resetting whole lines when a change occurs; monotype casts characters separately and is easier for single-character changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that small manuscript changes in linotype-set matter can trigger resetting many lines; this informs numbering choices (footnotes) and caution about mid-line edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation: legibility, size, one-sided, flat, and fastening
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be typewritten or in perfectly clear handwriting (typewritten preferable). Use uniform sheet size (desired dimension shown), use only one side, never roll manuscripts; place them flat in a box or envelope. Sheets should not be fastened except by pins or clips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fastening slips to a page use mucilage, not pins. Liberal top and left margins are required for reader/printer directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering and inserted/omitted pages marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages should be numbered consecutively. Inserted pages should be marked '4A', '4B' etc. Omitted pages should be indicated (e.g., number p.4 then '4-7'). Additions should be placed after the sheets to which they belong and labeled 'Insert A', 'Insert B' with margin instructions 'Here insert A.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear marking prevents misplacement and assists compositor tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph and footnote marking in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs should be plainly indicated either by indenting first line or by a ¶ mark. Footnotes should be clearly designated either by separating them from text with a line, using different color ink, or dedicating space via fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The in-text word carrying a note should be followed by a superior figure corresponding to the footnote. Footnotes should never be run into the text in manuscripts (even in parentheses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading workflow: use standard marks, answer queries, and minimize costly changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When marking proof-sheets use standard proofreaders' marks; answer all queries in the proofs; remember changes cost money and can necessitate resetting or repaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make manuscripts as perfect as possible before delivery. Alterations should be made in galley-proof stage to avoid costlier later corrections. Corrections in plates should be avoided as they are expensive and may injure plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and documentation of manuscript/proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The original manuscript should be returned with the galley-proof so the proofreader can refer to it if questions arise; each successive set of proofs returned should be accompanied by the previous marked set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists in calculating alteration costs and tracking changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to proofreaders: be authoritative, careful, discreet, and assume responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread as if you were the author; be careful about proper names and figures; look up unclear items or query the author; make queries clear and transfer manuscript queries to proofs; be discreet and avoid trivial criticisms; study editors' 'personal equation'; correct anything palpably wrong; do not follow copy blindly; the proofreader is the judge on correctness and style (learn Manual of Style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on author's or editor's 'OK' to relieve responsibility. Investigate when in doubt. Cultivate speed but prioritize accuracy. In rush cases protect yourself by disclaimers. Put your initial at the top of every galley read or revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints to copyholders: reading voice and enunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyholders should cultivate a low, soft, clear reading voice; small words are as essential as big ones; enunciate plural 's' distinctly; do not be offended when asked to repeat or when the reader inspects the copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good copyholding supports accurate proofreading and typesetting.
